curriculum: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics (CA CCSS-M) & CAASPP Smarter Balanced
organization: California Elementary Mathematics Open Curriculum Initiative

items.cluster: Count to tell the number of objects
items.title: Count Objects and Ten-Frames
items.prompt: How many red counters are shown on the ten-frame below?
items.explanation: Five counters fill the top row (a 5-group) and three fill the bottom row: 5 + 3 = 8.
items.hint: Count the 5 counters in the top row first, then add the 3 below.

items.cluster: Understand addition and subtraction
items.title: Adding Within 10
items.prompt: There are 4 frogs on a log and 3 frogs jump on. How many frogs in all?
items.explanation: Add 4 and 3 using a number bond: 4 + 3 = 7 frogs.
items.hint: Start at 4 and count forward 3 more: 5, 6, 7.

items.cluster: Understand addition and subtraction
items.title: Make 10 From Any Number (1–9)
items.prompt: Look at the ten-frame with 6 counters. How many more counters are needed to make a full 10?
items.explanation: 6 + 4 = 10. There are 4 empty spaces on the ten-frame.
items.hint: Count the empty boxes in the ten-frame.

items.cluster: Work with numbers 11-19 to gain foundations for place value
items.title: Compose and Decompose Teen Numbers (11–19)
items.prompt: In Eureka Math 'Say Ten' way, 1 ten and 7 ones is ten-7. What standard number is 10 + 7?
items.explanation: 1 ten (10) and 7 ones (7) compose the teen number 17: 10 + 7 = 17.
items.hint: Combine 10 and 7.

items.cluster: Identify and describe shapes
items.title: 2D Shape Identification
items.prompt: Which shape has exactly 3 straight sides and 3 corners (vertices)?
items.explanation: A triangle is defined as a closed polygon with exactly 3 sides and 3 angles.
items.hint: The prefix 'tri-' means three.

items.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction
items.title: Addition & Subtraction Word Problems within 20
items.prompt: Elena collected 14 seashells at Pismo Beach. Noah collected 8 seashells. How many FEWER seashells did Noah collect than Elena?
items.explanation: Compare using subtraction: 14 − 8 = 6 fewer seashells.
items.hint: Subtract 8 from 14 to find the difference.

items.cluster: Add and subtract within 20
items.title: Addition Fluency within 20 (Make a Ten)
items.prompt: What is 8 + 5?
items.explanation: Take 2 from 5 to make a 10 with 8: 8 + 2 = 10, then 10 + 3 = 13.
items.hint: Use the make-a-ten strategy: 8 + 2 = 10.

items.cluster: Understand place value
items.title: Tens and Ones Place Value
items.prompt: The number 47 has how many tens and how many ones?
items.explanation: In 47, the 4 is in the tens place (value 40) and the 7 is in the ones place.
items.hint: Look at the left digit for tens and the right digit for ones.

items.cluster: Tell and write time
items.title: Telling Time to Half Hour
items.prompt: When the short hour hand is halfway between 4 and 5, and the long minute hand points to 6, what time is it?
items.explanation: When the minute hand points to 6, 30 minutes have passed. The hour hand is past 4, so it is 4:30.
items.hint: Each number on the clock represents 5 minutes: 6 × 5 = 30 minutes.

items.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations
items.title: Addition within 1,000 with Regrouping
items.prompt: Calculate using vertical regrouping: 258 + 175
items.explanation: Add ones: 8+5=13 (write 3, bundle 1 ten). Add tens: 5+7+1=13 (write 3, bundle 1 hundred). Add hundreds: 2+1+1=4. Total = 433.
items.hint: Remember to bundle 10 ones into 1 ten and 10 tens into 1 hundred.

items.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction
items.title: Two-Step Word Problem
items.prompt: Maya had 50 markers. She gave 14 to Leo and 16 to Sam. How many markers does Maya have left?
items.explanation: Total given away: 14 + 16 = 30 markers. Remaining: 50 - 30 = 20 markers.
items.hint: First find how many markers were given away in total.

items.cluster: Work with time and money
items.title: Counting Money
items.prompt: What is the total value of 2 quarters, 3 dimes, and 4 pennies?
items.explanation: 2 quarters = 50¢. 3 dimes = 30¢. 4 pennies = 4¢. Total = 50 + 30 + 4 = 84¢.
items.hint: A quarter is 25¢, a dime is 10¢, and a penny is 1¢.

items.cluster: Represent and interpret data
items.title: Picture Graphs and Bar Graphs
items.prompt: Use the California Wildlife Bar Graph below: How many MORE Sea Otters were spotted than Bald Eagles?
items.explanation: Sea Otters = 13, Bald Eagles = 6. Subtract to compare: 13 − 6 = 7 more Sea Otters.
items.hint: Subtract the Bald Eagles bar from the Sea Otters bar.

items.cluster: Multiply and divide within 100
items.title: Multiplication Fact Fluency
items.prompt: What is 9 × 7?
items.explanation: 9 groups of 7 equals 63. You can also think (10 × 7) - 7 = 70 - 7 = 63.
items.hint: Think of 10 × 7 minus one group of 7.

items.cluster: Solve problems involving the four operations
items.title: Two-Step Word Problems (4 Operations)
items.prompt: A California citrus orchard packed 6 boxes with 8 oranges in each box, plus 15 loose oranges. How many oranges are there in all?
items.explanation: Step 1: 6 × 8 = 48 boxed oranges. Step 2: 48 + 15 = 63 total oranges.
items.hint: First multiply 6 × 8, then add 15.

items.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
items.title: Unit Fractions and Parts of a Whole
items.prompt: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Lucas eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza did Lucas eat?
items.explanation: The denominator is 8 (equal parts) and the numerator is 3 (parts eaten), making 3/8.
items.hint: The bottom number is the total number of equal slices.

items.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area
items.title: Area of a Rectangle
items.prompt: A classroom rug is 8 feet long and 6 feet wide. What is its area in square feet?
items.explanation: Area of a rectangle = length × width. 8 ft × 6 ft = 48 square feet.
items.hint: Multiply the length by the width.

items.cluster: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems
items.title: Multi-Step Word Problems & Remainder Interpretation
items.prompt: 58 fourth-grade students are taking vans to the California Science Center. Each van holds 8 students. What is the MINIMUM number of vans needed so every student gets a seat?
items.explanation: Seven vans seat 8 × 7 = 56 students. Since 58 - 56 = 2 students remain, one more van is needed: 7 + 1 = 8 vans.
items.hint: Divide 58 by 8. Can the 2 remaining students be left behind?

items.cluster: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence
items.title: Equivalent Fractions
items.prompt: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
items.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2: (3×2)/(4×2) = 6/8.
items.hint: Multiply both the top and bottom by 2.

items.cluster: Use place value understanding to perform multi-digit arithmetic
items.title: Multi-Digit Multiplication
items.prompt: Compute using an area model or partial products: 24 × 15
items.explanation: Use the distributive property: 24 × 10 = 240, and 24 × 5 = 120. 240 + 120 = 360.
items.hint: Break 15 into 10 + 5 and multiply each part by 24.

items.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion
items.title: Perimeter and Area Formulas
items.prompt: A rectangular garden has a perimeter of 30 meters. If the length is 9 meters, what is the width?
items.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (L + W) = 30. L + W = 15. If L = 9, then W = 15 - 9 = 6 meters.
items.hint: Two lengths equal 18 m. Subtract 18 from 30, then divide by 2.

items.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles
items.title: Additive Angle Measure (Complementary & Supplementary)
items.prompt: A right angle (90°) is decomposed into two non-overlapping angles. One angle measures 38°. What is the measure of the other angle?
items.explanation: Complementary angles sum to 90°: 90° − 38° = 52°.
items.hint: Subtract 38° from 90°.

items.cluster: Write and interpret numerical expressions
items.title: Order of Operations (PEMDAS)
items.prompt: Evaluate: 4 + (6 × 3) - 2
items.explanation: 1. Parentheses: 6 × 3 = 18. 2. Addition & subtraction left to right: 4 + 18 - 2 = 20.
items.hint: Perform the operation inside the parentheses first.

items.cluster: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions
items.title: Adding Fractions with Unlike Denominators
items.prompt: What is 1/3 + 2/5?
items.hint: Find the least common multiple of 3 and 5, which is 15.

items.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division
items.title: Fractions as Division (a ÷ b = a/b)
items.prompt: 5 friends equally share 3 identical pans of cornbread. What fraction of a pan does each friend receive?
items.explanation: By CA CCSS-M 5.NF.B.3, a ÷ b = a/b. Dividing 3 pans among 5 friends gives 3 ÷ 5 = 3/5 of a pan each.
items.hint: Divide the number of pans Being Shared (3) by the number of Sharers (5).

items.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume
items.title: Volume of Right Rectangular Prisms
items.prompt: A storage container is 5 meters long, 4 meters wide, and 3 meters high. What is its volume?
items.explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cubic meters.
items.hint: Multiply length × width × height.

items.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume
items.title: Additive Volume of Composite Solid Figures
items.prompt: An L-shaped sculpture base is made of two non-overlapping rectangular prisms. Prism A is 4 ft × 3 ft × 2 ft. Prism B is 5 ft × 2 ft × 3 ft. What is the total volume?
items.explanation: Volume is additive: V_A = 4×3×2 = 24 cu ft. V_B = 5×2×3 = 30 cu ft. Total V = 24 + 30 = 54 cu ft.
items.hint: Calculate the volume of Prism A and Prism B separately, then add them together.
